mode: scenario-adaptation; no upstream implementation or harness copied

mbuf-release.adaptation: Use Ker pool; require restored availability instead of skip.

clock-monotonic.adaptation: Use Ker monotonic nanosecond clock; no ff TSC implementation.

empty-export.adaptation: Verify zero-length copy export and ownership, not NIC transmission.

null-context.adaptation: Ker allocation rejects null context; no upstream ff consumption rule.

packet-export.adaptation: Verify copied bytes and lifetime; no ethdev send claim.

multiseg-boundary.adaptation: Ker currently rejects multi-segment adoption, preserving caller ownership; positive support deferred.

queue-isolation.adaptation: Two owner-worker Linux skb FIFOs; no reload generations or SP/SC DPDK ring claim.

queue-full-ownership.adaptation: Full FIFO preserves caller reference and pool availability; no drain-ring statistics claim.

export-exhaustion-retry.adaptation: Exhaust the real Ker packet pool, assert failed copy-out preserves the caller's output slot and skb ownership, then release one mbuf and require a successful retry. No mocked copydata or NIC send claim.

offload-metadata-rejection.adaptation: Ker explicitly rejects checksum-partial and GSO metadata it cannot export, preserves the skb and output slot, then succeeds after metadata is cleared. No offload execution claim.

software-checksum-completion.adaptation: Ker-specific software completion extension motivated by this upstream checksum-offload case: copy a linear Internet-checksum CHECKSUM_PARTIAL skb and complete its seeded transport checksum using Linux checksum primitives before export. CRC32C is rejected when the imported skb layout exposes csum_not_inet; GSO and the existing ordinary CHECKSUM_PARTIAL export remain rejected, and the copy carries no DPDK TX offload flags. This does not claim F-Stack's NIC/hardware offload behavior.

headroom-export.adaptation: Export a payload with explicit headroom, verify mbuf data_off and bytes, then free the skb and validate copy lifetime. No ethdev transmission claim.

multiseg-copy.adaptation: Use a real three-segment DPDK chain with uneven and zero-length segments as input to Ker's explicit chain-to-linear-skb copy adapter; verify source links/refcounts remain caller-owned and the copy survives source-chain release. This does not implement upstream's segmented TX path or Linux nonlinear skb support.

multiseg-ethernet-ingress.adaptation: Adapt the multisegment packet geometry intent in the ingress direction: split destination/source/type fields across real DPDK segments, copy to a linear skb, classify with unchanged Linux eth_type_trans and deliver one host packet through Ker's existing protocol runtime. Also verify broadcast/otherhost classification, ownership and failure boundaries. This is not F-Stack TX, NIC traffic, Ethernet offload or nonlinear Linux skb support.

arp-chain-feedback.adaptation: Ker-specific integration extension of the upstream multisegment geometry scenario: split a valid Ethernet ARP reply across a real DPDK chain, linearize and classify it, then exercise the existing ARP decoder and scoped native neighbor feedback from an actual worker RX poll. Verify rejection boundaries, timer/reference preservation, source-chain release and pool recovery. The ARP feedback scenario is not an upstream F-Stack test and does not claim NIC traffic or general ARP learning. The opt-in known-peer resolver extension also tests INCOMPLETE reply admission, queued output, invalid broadcast reply retention, and consumed output on exporter pressure through the same actual worker RX path.

ipv4-ingress-validation.adaptation: Ker-specific ingress/header-validation extension. At pinned F-Stack revision 646a641cfff77f4815e1e29829a09e1ed15a2999 both named cases exercise ff_dpdk_if_send, not IPv4 ingress. Ker uses real segmented DPDK input and its copy/classify path, then validates IPv4 header/options, length, padding and native ip_fast_csum. No ip_rcv, routing, fragment reassembly, transport/socket or NIC delivery claim.

udp-ingress-validation.adaptation: Ker-specific ingress extension motivated by the pinned UDP checksum TX case. The F-Stack source only sets UDP TX offload metadata and calls ff_dpdk_if_send; it does not test UDP ingress. Ker validates an unfragmented IPv4 UDP datagram using the original Linux pseudoheader checksum primitives. This does not claim socket delivery, routing, reassembly, ICMP, NIC or TX offload support.

udp-minimal-boundaries.adaptation: Additional Ker-specific UDP ingress regression for the minimum eight-byte header with zero and valid nonzero checksums, zero-valued ports, even payload length and Ethernet padding exclusion. The upstream case is still TX-only and does not cover these receive semantics.

tcp-ingress-validation.adaptation: Ker-specific ingress extension motivated by the pinned TCP checksum TX case. The upstream case enables TCP TX checksum offload and calls ff_dpdk_if_send; it is not a TCP receive test. Ker validates an unfragmented IPv4 TCP segment and its complete pseudoheader checksum, preserving options as opaque bytes. This does not claim TCP option interpretation, connection state, routing, reassembly, socket delivery, NIC or TX offload support.

transport-receive.adaptation: Ker-specific worker RX integration extension motivated by upstream UDP/TCP TX checksum-offload cases; neither upstream case tests ingress. A registered ETH_P_IP handler validates and synchronously exposes existing immutable UDP/TCP packet views, consumes its skb reference on every path, and fails closed when protocol fanout shares the skb descriptor reference. This is not socket delivery, routing, fragment reassembly, TCP state or NIC receive support.

icmp-echo.adaptation: Ker-specific ICMPv4 echo constructor and worker-ingress extension. The pinned F-Stack cases cover UDP/TCP TX checksum offload, not ICMP. Ker constructs explicit-address echo request/reply frames with opaque IPv4 options and validates the complete ICMP checksum in an immutable worker callback view; it does not implement automatic replies, ICMP errors, routing, reassembly, sockets, ping or NIC support.

udp-create.adaptation: Ker-specific software packet-construction and receive-roundtrip extension motivated by the upstream UDP TX checksum-offload case, which is not an explicit-address UDP constructor or ingress scenario. Ker builds a fixed Ethernet/IPv4/UDP packet with Linux software checksum primitives, copies it through the existing export and segmented ingress adapters, then validates it in the worker-scoped transport receiver. No routing, address policy, socket, automatic TX offload or NIC transmission is claimed.

udp-configured-create.adaptation: Ker-specific explicit-address constructor extension motivated by the pinned F-Stack UDP checksum TX case; upstream does not test configured address snapshots. Source IPv4/MAC come from the one live configured Ethernet IPv4 address, while destination MAC/IP are caller literals. Independent wire oracles cover opaque IPv4 options and zero/DF field profiles, allocation rollback, and raw-constructor byte equivalence. No neighbor lookup, route/FIB selection, socket delivery, NIC/offload, or source-address-selection policy is implied.

tcp-configured-create.adaptation: Ker-specific configured-source TCP/IPv4 constructor extension motivated by the pinned F-Stack TCP checksum TX case; upstream does not test configured address snapshots. Source IPv4/MAC come from one live configured Ethernet IPv4 address and destination MAC/IP are caller literals. Independent wire checks cover both opaque option areas, TCP checksum semantics including a zero checksum result, allocation rollback and raw-constructor byte equivalence. No neighbor lookup, route/FIB selection, TCP state, socket delivery, NIC or hardware offload is implied.

icmp-echo-configured-create.adaptation: Ker-specific configured-source ICMP echo constructor extension motivated by the pinned UDP checksum TX case; upstream does not test ICMP or configured source snapshots. Source IPv4/MAC come from one live configured Ethernet IPv4 address and destination MAC/IP are caller literals. Independent wire checks validate the complete IPv4 and ICMP checksums for opaque options and zero/DF profiles, including a folded-zero ICMP checksum. The test also verifies shared UDP/TCP/ICMP address-association failure rollback. No neighbor lookup, route/FIB selection, automatic reply, ICMP errors, socket delivery or NIC/offload is implied.

udp-neighbor-create.adaptation: Ker-specific neighbor-backed packet-construction extension motivated by the pinned UDP TX checksum case. The upstream case does not perform neighbor selection or ARP resolution. Ker uses one configured local address/device and an existing permanent neighbor entry, releases the lookup reference before allocating the packet, then validates software checksum and worker RX copy/retry behavior. No unresolved queue, ARP resolution, FIB, route, socket or NIC transmission is claimed.

tx-copy-export-retry.adaptation: Ker-specific worker TX copy/retry extension motivated by the pinned UDP checksum TX case. A bounded owner-worker FIFO retains each original skb until a sink accepts its checksum-completed or ordinary private mbuf copy; failures retry the pending head and cancellation returns ownership. The sink is an application copy consumer, not an ethdev/NIC, and no hardware offload or F-Stack TX path is claimed.

tcp-create.adaptation: Ker-specific explicit-address TCP/IPv4 packet-construction and worker receive-roundtrip extension motivated by the pinned TCP TX checksum-offload case, which is not a constructor or receive test. Ker writes fixed Ethernet/IPv4/TCP headers and software checksums; an application sink accepts a copy, then a real segmented chain is classified and validated by the existing TCP packet-view receiver. No socket, TCP state machine, route, NIC or hardware offload is claimed.

tcp-options-create.adaptation: Ker-specific extension of the pinned TCP TX checksum case: constructs fixed IPv4 headers with copied opaque TCP options and validates the software checksum through the worker receive path. The upstream case does not test option construction or interpretation. Options are not parsed, and this adds no TCP state, routing, socket, NIC or hardware offload support.

tcp-neighbor-create.adaptation: Ker-specific extension of the pinned TCP TX checksum case: derives the source IPv4/MAC from one configured address/device and the destination MAC from an existing NUD_PERMANENT neighbor, releases the lookup reference before allocation, then validates software checksums through TX retry and segmented worker RX. The upstream case does not test neighbor selection or ARP resolution. No unresolved queue, FIB, routing, source fallback, TCP state, socket or NIC transmission is claimed.

fstack-chain-export.adaptation: Ker-specific positive linear-skb-to-DPDK-chain copy extension motivated by the pinned multisegment TX case. Ker copies an existing supported linear UDP/TCP packet into independently owned direct mbufs, then validates the chain through its copy/classify worker RX path after releasing the source skb. The upstream case exercises F-Stack TX; this does not claim F-Stack/NIC transmission, Linux nonlinear skb support, or offload.

tx-chain-export.adaptation: Ker-specific worker TX copy extension motivated by the pinned multisegment TX case. Opt-in chain mode exports a supported linear skb into a direct DPDK chain and gives the whole chain to an application sink only on acceptance; a rejected copy is freed while the original FIFO skb remains pending for retry. This is not native F-Stack/NIC TX, Linux nonlinear skb support, or hardware offload. Chain mode accepts CHECKSUM_NONE only; the existing legacy exporter retains its separate software CHECKSUM_PARTIAL path.

tx-ring-drain.adaptation: Ker-specific application-ring transport extension motivated by the pinned multisegment TX case. The worker exporter submits whole copied chains to an exact-capacity DPDK ring configured for one producer and one consumer; a ring-full result preserves the original skb for retry, while the consumer validates and drains accepted chains through Ker's existing Ethernet copy/classify and worker transport receive path. The upstream test exercises F-Stack TX. This does not claim an ethdev, NIC/RSS, multi-process ring, or F-Stack TX integration.

rx-ring-drain.adaptation: Ker-specific worker RX extension over the application ring: one attached consumer copies accepted direct chains into owned Linux skbs and dispatches them through the existing Ethernet and IPv4 transport receive path. Allocation pressure retains the popped chain for retry; option-bearing UDP/TCP frames preserve FIFO order through allocation retry and explicit pending-chain cancellation. ICMP echo is delivered by the same worker path, while a bad ICMP checksum is consumed as a drop without invoking the callback. This does not implement ethdev RX, NIC/RSS, NAPI polling, multi-process sharing, or sockets.

fstack-chain-software-checksum.adaptation: Ker-specific software-completion extension motivated by the pinned IPv4 UDP/TCP checksum TX cases: completes a linear CHECKSUM_PARTIAL skb with the existing Linux checksum semantics, copies it into direct DPDK segments (including a checksum field split across segment boundaries), then validates it through native Ethernet classification and the actual worker transport receiver. This regression set also places checksum start after variable IPv4 IHL/options for both UDP and TCP. The upstream cases exercise TX checksum offload; this does not claim NIC or hardware offload, nonlinear Linux skb support, sockets, or TCP state.

tx-chain-software-checksum.adaptation: Ker-specific worker TX extension motivated by pinned UDP/TCP TX checksum cases. An explicit exporter mode admits CHECKSUM_NONE and supported Internet CHECKSUM_PARTIAL packets, completes partial checksums in a private direct-chain copy, and preserves the original skb on sink rejection for retry. Tests verify checksum bytes through the actual worker receive path. The upstream cases exercise offload; this does not claim NIC/hardware offload, nonlinear Linux skb support, sockets, or TCP state.

cross-worker-ring-rx.adaptation: Ker-specific same-process SP/SC worker extension motivated by the pinned multisegment TX case. Worker A exports UDP/TCP chains to a DPDK ring; a distinct EAL worker B uses its own packet pool, skb context, device, and actual worker RX poll to classify and validate the packets. Pool pressure retains the FIFO head for retry. Lifecycle changes require external quiescence. The upstream case exercises F-Stack TX; this does not claim RSS steering, multiprocess rings, NIC I/O, or F-Stack RX.

fstack-concurrent-ring.adaptation: Ker-specific concurrent same-process SP/SC extension motivated by pinned F-Stack segmented TX and UDP/TCP checksum TX cases. A registered EAL producer and distinct registered EAL consumer overlap across 192 alternating UDP, TCP, and ICMP echo chains using a capacity-one DPDK ring; an independent wire-byte checksum oracle runs before enqueue and the actual consumer worker validates protocol dispatch order and payloads. IPv4 and TCP option lengths vary across the records. Initial backpressure is deterministic. This does not claim MPMC, multiprocess/RSS, NIC I/O, F-Stack RX, or upstream concurrency coverage.

udp-ip-options.adaptation: Ker-specific extension: construct explicit Ethernet/IPv4/UDP packets with opaque copied IPv4 options, validate the variable-IHL IPv4 and UDP checksums, then export a segmented copy through the actual worker receive path. The pinned cases motivate checksum and segmented-buffer coverage; they do not test IPv4 options semantics. No routing, source-route processing, socket delivery or NIC transmission is claimed.

tcp-ip-options.adaptation: Ker-specific extension constructs Ethernet/IPv4/TCP packets with independently supplied opaque IPv4 and TCP option bytes, verifies both checksums with independent wire-byte oracles, and sends a segmented copy through the actual worker receive path. Existing constructors remain zero-IP-options wrappers. The pinned F-Stack cases motivate checksum and segmented-buffer coverage, not IPv4/TCP option semantics; no routing, source-route processing, TCP state, sockets or NIC transmission is claimed.

udp-neighbor-ip-options.adaptation: Ker-specific neighbor-backed construction extension: copy opaque IPv4 options into a UDP packet derived from one configured local address/device and an existing permanent neighbor; verify variable-IHL and UDP checksums, reference release before allocation, rollback and worker RX retry. The pinned upstream case is TX checksum-only and does not cover neighbor selection or options. No ARP resolution, routing, source fallback, sockets or NIC transmission.

tcp-neighbor-headers.adaptation: Ker-specific combined neighbor-construction extension: copy independent opaque IPv4 and TCP options (including 40-byte areas), verify both checksums and lookup-reference release before allocation, then exercise worker TX/RX retry. The pinned upstream case is TX checksum-only and does not cover neighbor selection or options. No option interpretation, ARP resolution, routing, TCP state, sockets or NIC transmission.

icmp-neighbor-create.adaptation: Ker-specific ICMP echo constructor extension motivated by the pinned UDP checksum TX case; upstream does not test ICMP or neighbor selection. It uses one configured local address/device and an existing permanent neighbor, releases the lookup reference before allocation, and checks opaque IPv4 options and full ICMP checksum through TX retry and actual worker RX. This does not implement ARP resolution, routing, automatic replies, ICMP errors, sockets, ping, or NIC transmission.

icmp-chain-exact-fold.adaptation: Ker-specific exact-fold checksum-copy extension motivated by segmented TX and checksum cases. An explicit opt-in chain mode preserves a folded zero in a private CHECKSUM_PARTIAL checksum completion; the existing checksum mode retains its zero-mangling behavior. ICMP echo packets verify the exact checksum through segmented worker RX and ring backpressure. This is software completion, not NIC offload, automatic ICMP response, or a claim about general protocol zero-mangling policy.

ipv4-field-profiles.adaptation: Ker-specific constructor extension motivated by pinned IPv4 UDP/TCP checksum and segmented-TX cases; those upstream cases do not test IPv4 DS/ID/fragment-field construction. Ker copies an explicit opaque DS byte and wire-order identification into UDP/TCP/ICMP echo frames, admits only fragment field zero or DF, and independently verifies IPv4 plus transport checksums. Permanent-neighbor variants reuse the configured source/neighbor snapshot path; a concurrent 192-packet three-protocol worker-ring case verifies field preservation. An RX-ring case carries a DF profile through exact software checksum completion, allocation-pressure cancellation and FIFO recovery. Legacy constructors remain byte-identical zero-profile wrappers. This does not implement DSCP/ECN policy, ID generation, fragmentation, PMTU, routing, or NIC behavior.

arp-configured.source_case: RFC 826 section 2 ARP packet format (Ker-specific constructor extension)
arp-configured.adaptation: Checks the 42-byte Ethernet/ARP request and reply formats against an independent wire-byte oracle, including explicit broadcast destination and zero target hardware address for requests, and verifies byte-equivalence with Ker's existing raw adapter. RFC 826 reference: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc826. No neighbor lookup, routing, automatic reply, or NIC transmission is implied. The separate existing arp-receive test covers DAD, Ethernet padding, malformed packets, callback ownership, and copied-message lifetime; this batch adds a segmented padded-DAD regression through the unchanged decoder.

arp-ring.adaptation: Ker-specific integration extension motivated by the pinned F-Stack segmented-ring TX case; upstream has no ARP test. Configured 42-byte requests/replies travel as real DPDK chains through worker TX export, a bounded ring, actual worker RX polling, Ethernet classification and the original ARP receiver. It checks retry ownership, existing scoped feedback rejection/acceptance, short-frame drops, and pool-pressure cancellation/FIFO recovery. This does not claim general ARP learning, automatic response, NIC/RSS, or F-Stack RX.

arp-concurrent-ring.adaptation: Ker-specific same-process SP/SC extension motivated by the pinned F-Stack segmented-ring TX case; upstream has no ARP test. Distinct configured request/reply frames cross a capacity-one ring between separate EAL workers; the consumer uses its own packet pool/context/device and actual worker RX dispatcher to verify all 192 records in FIFO order. This does not claim MPMC, multiprocess/RSS, NIC I/O, or a general ARP protocol stack.

configured-ring.adaptation: Ker-specific configured-source integration extension. Configured UDP, TCP and ICMP echo constructors pass through software checksum export, a real bounded DPDK ring, Ethernet classification and the actual worker transport receiver; independent corruption cases cover bad IPv4/UDP checksums, fragments and unsupported protocols. A pool-pressure case cancels the exact pending chain and resumes the later FIFO entry, and ARP plus IPv4 handlers share one configured device/runtime with cleanup pins checked. The pinned F-Stack cases motivate checksum and segmented TX coverage, not configured-source selection, ARP, or ingress. No routing, automatic ARP, sockets, NIC I/O, or F-Stack RX is claimed.

flow-receive.adaptation: Ker-specific steering/ingress extension motivated by the pinned segmented TX scenario. Segmented IPv4 UDP/TCP chains pass through fixed owner selection and local or worker-poll handoff, then the owner uses its separate pool/context/device for Ethernet copy/classification and transport checksum validation. Includes capacity-one inbox retry, bad-checksum drops, and explicit callback-owned allocation-failure drop/recovery. Logical workers share one EAL thread. The upstream case does not test steering or ingress; this does not claim RSS, NIC I/O, sockets, TCP state, production retry buffering, or IPv6 transport reception. The companion flow-chain test covers IPv4/IPv6 segmented parsing and handoff ownership. Extended to every IPv4 option length from 0 through 40 bytes, validating copied option bytes, full header length, options-area checksum corruption and recovery; flow-ip-options separately checks variable-IHL steering bounds and fixed key/hash invariance. Options remain opaque, without source-route or other option interpretation. The input now enters through a real bounded ker_tx_ring and ker_flow_ring worker RX callback, which preserves a pending chain on full owner inbox and retries before reading later entries. This ingress ownership retry does not change the explicit owner-side allocation-drop policy.

flow-concurrent-receive.adaptation: Ker-specific complete flow ingress/owner receive integration inspired by the pinned segmented TX case. Two distinct pinned CPUs run ingress ring steering and owner-local Ethernet/IPv4 TCP/UDP validation with separate pools and receive state. Immutable expected records verify packet/key bytes and callback placement, deterministic full-inbox pending/FIFO retry, checksum drops, owner-pool exhaustion/drop/recovery, and orderly drain/teardown. Skip only with fewer than two allowed CPUs; setup errors fail. This does not claim upstream F-Stack flow coverage, NIC/RSS, sockets, TCP state, or a production allocation-retry bridge.

flow-owner-receive.adaptation: Ker-specific owner receive adapter inspired by the pinned segmented TX scenario. A bounded owner-local packet ring queues chains after flow handoff; worker service polling reuses the Ethernet copy/classify receive path. Destination allocation failure retains one pending chain for FIFO retry; queue overflow explicitly consumes and drops the newest chain. Tests cover allocation recovery during RX pressure, lifecycle pins, cancellation and initialization rollback. This is not upstream F-Stack flow coverage, end-to-end lossless backpressure, NIC/RSS, sockets or TCP state.

neighbor-resolved-output.adaptation: Ker-specific native Linux resolved-neighbor output extension, motivated by the pinned packet-send scenario. The neighbor-timer test sends configured IPv4 frames through unchanged neigh_resolve_output and native event-send inline bodies into the bounded TX exporter. It checks current neighbor MAC header rebuilding, supported NUD states and native timer transitions, TX ownership and retries, and admission failures. Source provenance for the three Linux bodies is verified separately by neighbor-output-import. No upstream F-Stack neighbor test, unknown-neighbor resolution, routing, sockets or NIC transmission is claimed.

neighbor-known-peer-resolution.adaptation: Ker-specific native Linux neighbor re-resolution extension: previously monitored known peer enters INCOMPLETE, queues bounded skb ownership, solicits through explicit ARP callbacks, and flushes via unchanged neighbor update after accepted feedback. Exercises queue pressure, timeout and cancellation. The F-Stack source case motivates packet output only; it is not an upstream neighbor-resolution test and does not establish unknown-peer discovery, routing, sockets or NIC transmission.

neighbor-discovery.adaptation: Ker-specific first-contact neighbor discovery extension: explicitly create a bounded NUD_NONE peer without a supplied MAC, drive native resolution with outbound packets, and consume valid worker ARP feedback to flush queued data. Tests initialization rollback and owned-entry lifecycle. The F-Stack source motivates packet output, not neighbor discovery; full Linux neighbor creation, routing, general ARP learning, sockets and NIC transmission remain outside this slice.

arp-responder.adaptation: Ker-specific responder and two-peer discovery integration extension: the production responder builds a local ARP reply with the native constructor, actual application rings/worker RX deliver it to the discovery peer, and native neighbor output releases queued UDP for transport validation. Tests bounded failures, reply selection and ownership. These upstream cases motivate packet output/segmentation, not an F-Stack ARP responder; full arp_process, general learning, routing and NIC transmission are not claimed.

icmp-echo-service.adaptation: Ker-specific first-contact echo-service integration extension. Two independent skb pools and real SP/SC rings carry a validated echo request, native neighbor resolution emits an ARP probe through the existing responder and scoped feedback path, and the returned echo reply is checked by the peer transport callback. This is not the F-Stack socket, ping, full ICMP input/reply path, routing, or NIC delivery.

icmpv4-service.adaptation: Ker-specific ICMPv4 control extension: generic error events, bounded safe error emission, timestamp and opt-in extended echo, token-bucket limits and independent peer pools with actual RX/TX rings. The source cases motivate packet delivery only; no upstream ICMP suite, sockets, routing, IPv4 reassembly, IPv6 or NIC delivery is claimed. The same real-ring fixture also exercises an opt-in bounded Ker UDP endpoint table: validated local datagrams reach bound callbacks, while lookup misses automatically generate ICMP port-unreachable through the existing neighbor output. This is not native Linux socket lookup or a F-Stack UDP ingress test. Explicit immutable unavailable-protocol declarations additionally drive automatic ICMP protocol-unreachable for validated local IPv4 ingress, with competing-handler suppression. This is a Ker policy adapter, not Linux inet_protos/raw socket/XFRM integration. Connected endpoint regressions extend the Ker-specific UDP adapter with generation-scoped handles and exact peer filtering; these are not upstream F-Stack socket tests.

icmpv4-pmtu.adaptation: Ker-specific path-MTU extension: require a sent-packet confirmation callback before lowering one peer cache, apply legacy plateaus and expiry, and reject actual oversized neighbor output without taking packet ownership. This is not a F-Stack PMTU test and does not add routing, sockets, retransmission, segmentation or IPv6.

udp-io.adaptation: Ker-specific bounded UDP datagram I/O extension, using actual EAL, packet pools, UDP constructors, neighbor output, TX exporter and RX ring dispatcher. Caller-owned RX slots copy tuple and payload and cover truncation, peek, zero-length datagrams, packet/byte limits and recovery. An exact peer registry supports connected send and explicit sendto without changing the receive filter. Real TX ring and queue pressure validate retry and allocation ownership; MTU callback reentry and lifecycle pins are rejected. This is not a F-Stack socket test, host-socket interoperability, NIC/RSS, multicast or fragmentation support.

udp-error.adaptation: Ker-specific asynchronous UDP error extension. Real UDP construction, neighbor output, TX copy/sink acceptance and ICMP receive dispatch establish exact quoted IPv4/UDP evidence. Bounded RESERVED/SENT records reject unsent, forged, stale-generation and stale-incarnation errors; per-channel queues expose copied errno/tuple/reporter/MTU data. Tests cover alternate peers, PMTU reduction and expiry, error-queue bounds, reservation recovery and callback/lifetime failures. Sink acceptance is application-level evidence, not NIC completion or peer delivery; this is not a F-Stack upstream socket/ICMP test and does not provide cryptographic ICMP authentication.
